text:
Jordan Kyrou spent 488 games as a Blue before landing in Washington, and his first month as a Capital has been loud: 14 points in 16 games, seven of them on the power play, in under 15 minutes a night.

Some of that is real. Evolving-Hockey had him driving play and suppressing chances at an elite rate last season (96th and 99th percentile among forwards), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries and living in the home-plate area. He gets to the good ice.

The finishing is the part to discount. He has five goals on 2.2 expected and is shooting 21%, against 10% last season. His last two games produced no shots at all. The playmaking (nine assists) and the power-play role look sturdier than the goal total.

What we'd watch: his ice time, which has crept up to 15.4 minutes over the last ten. If Washington keeps feeding him minutes, the points can hold even when the shooting cools.
headline: Kyrou's Washington start runs hot
